عَسْجَدٌ , an instance of a quadriliteral-radical word without any letter of the kind termed ذَوْلَقِىٌّ; (S, O, TA;) the letters of this kind being six; three pronounced with the tip of the tongue, namely, ر and ل and ن; and three labial, namely, ب and ف and م; (TA;) Gold: (S, O, K:) and (as some say, O, TA) any gems, such as pearls and يَاقُوت [or sapphires]. (O, K.) ＝
-A2- Also A large, or bulky, camel: (O, K:) a small one is called لَطِيمٌ. (TA.) ―
-b2- And, accord. to AZ, A certain stallion-camel. (O.) See also the following paragraph.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
